chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, all together from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithammi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Munthir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three will be punished on the Day of Resurrection: a man who lied in his dream, he will be commanded to tie a knot between two grains, and he will not be able to tie a knot between them; and a man who created images, he will be commanded to breathe into them, and he will not be able to breathe into them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for lying in dreams and creating images in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the sin of false dreamers and image-makers to the concept of *tasyir* (imitating creation), a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding the prohibition of statues. The eschatological punishment of performing an impossible task—such as tying a knot between two grains or breathing life into an inanimate object—serves as a metaphor for the futility of their claim to creative power. This narration is frequently cited in discussions on the spiritual consequences of visual arts and the preservation of divine uniqueness (*Tawhid*).

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, altogether from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysmi, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Husayn Bin Al Munzar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three would be Punished on the Day of Judgement – a man who lied regarding his dream, he would be Encumbered to tie a knot between two grains, and he would not be able to tie a knot between the two; and a man who images resemblances, he would be Encumbered that he blows (a spirit) into it, and he would not be able to blow into it’. (P.s. – the description of the third is missing).
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah all from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy, from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from al-Husayn ibn al-Mundhir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith. ‘Three kinds of people will be in suffering on the Day of Judgment. Of such people, one is a man who lies about his dream. He will be held responsible to form a knot between two pieces of barley grains and he will never be able to do so. One is a man who builds statues. He will be held responsible to blow the spirit in it and he will never be able to do so.’” (The third according to al-Saduq is one who listens to a people who do not like him. Lead will be poured in his ears.)
